newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ELECTRICITY HIGHER ON WEATHER, PHYSICALS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ELECTRICITY HIGHER ON WEATHER, PHYSICALS.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were higher Monday on hot weather forecasts for parts of the West and some strength in the physical power market, industry sources said.
As of 1240 EDT, September Palo Verde (PV) was up $1.13 at the day's high of $32.90 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges as low as $32.00, while October was up 15 cents at $24.25 per MWh.

September California Oregon Border (COB) was up 65 cents at the day's high of $24.05 after trading as low as $23.85, while October was up 45 cents at the day's high of $23.40 after exchanges as low as $23.00 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1200 EDT an estimated total of 111 PV and 49 COB contracts had traded.
Day-ahead firm peak prices in the West were generally said to be firmer, quoted at $42.00-44.00 at PV and $21.00-22.50 per MWh at COB.
Strength was said to be coming from forecasts of hot weather in parts of the West.
Forecasters called for the Northwest to run two to six degrees Fahrenheit above normal with well below normal precipitation.
Temperatures in western section of the Southwest would remain three to six degrees above normal and the east section was expected to be as much as five degrees below normal.

The 750 megawatt (MW) unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico, shut late Thursday for repairs, was back to full power by late Saturday, a spokeswoman for the plant said Monday.
The plant's other 750 MW unit, as well as its 220 MW and two 185 MW units, were said to be operating normally.
